findings.situation: A service member moved under permanent-change-of-station orders in late 2024, paid unreimbursed moving costs in 2025, and can deduct them on the 2025 line 14, but truthfully answers No because the question asks only about a 2025 move.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 93, Line 14: "You can deduct moving expenses if you are a member of the Armed Forces on active duty and due to a military order you move because of a permanent change of station."
findings.why: The tax text does not limit the deduction to a move made in 2025. Because the question says "a 2025 move", expenses for an earlier move that fall in 2025 get a No, so the interview goes on without a deduction the filer may take.

findings.situation: A reservist or National Guard member who was not on active duty moved to a new permanent post under military orders and truthfully answers Yes, so the interview ends even though line 14 does not allow this deduction.
findings.source_text: Question: "moving costs, not paid back, of a 2025 move to a new permanent post under military orders"; i1040gi p. 93, Line 14: "if you are a member of the Armed Forces on active duty and due to a military order you move because of a permanent change of station"
findings.why: The question leaves out the active-duty condition. Its gate also counts any service since 2022, including reserves and Guard. So a Yes covers situations the line does not allow.

locators: Form 1040 (2025), lines 8, 10, 13b, 16, 19–20 and 27–31; , Line 14, "If you are claiming only storage fees during your absence from the United States, check the box on line 14"
